findings.title: SqlCommand runs SQL built from strings
findings.why: If any part comes from a request, an attacker can change the query (SQL injection).
findings.fix: Use command parameters (@name) instead of putting values into the SQL text.

findings.title: 'ConnectionString' holds a value written in the code
findings.why: Anyone with the code (or a leaked copy) gets the secret, and it can't be rotated without a release.
findings.fix: Read it from configuration or a secret store; rotate the exposed value.

findings.title: 'apiKey' holds a value written in the code
findings.why: Anyone with the code (or a leaked copy) gets the secret, and it can't be rotated without a release.
findings.fix: Read it from configuration or a secret store; rotate the exposed value.

findings.title: POST /orders changes data without sign-in
findings.why: Anyone who can reach the API can call it. Writes are the first thing an attacker tries.
findings.fix: Add .RequireAuthorization() (or the project's key guard) to the endpoint or its group.

findings.title: Requests over plain HTTP are not redirected to HTTPS
findings.why: Keys, cookies and data can travel unencrypted and be read on the way.

findings.title: Authorization runs before authentication
findings.why: Policies are checked before the user is known, so they can fail open or always deny.

findings.title: Endpoints ask for rate limits but the limiter isn't in the pipeline
findings.why: The limits are silently not applied.
findings.fix: Add app.UseRateLimiter() after routing and authentication.

findings.title: MD5 is used
findings.why: MD5 is broken for security uses: collisions can be forged.
findings.fix: Use SHA256 or better; for passwords use a password hasher (PBKDF2, bcrypt, Argon2).

findings.title: POST /auth/login is public and has no rate limit
findings.why: A public route without a limit can be flooded to slow the app down or to run up hosting costs.
findings.fix: Add .RequireRateLimiting("<policy>") with a policy partitioned by client.

findings.title: POST /auth/login looks like a sign-in or token route but has no rate limit
findings.why: Without a limit, passwords and codes can be guessed by brute force.
findings.fix: Rate-limit by user and by IP, and lock out after repeated failures.

findings.title: POST /orders is public and has no rate limit
findings.why: A public route without a limit can be flooded to slow the app down or to run up hosting costs.
findings.fix: Add .RequireRateLimiting("<policy>") with a policy partitioned by client.

findings.title: Browsers aren't told to insist on HTTPS (no HSTS)
findings.why: A first visit over HTTP can be intercepted and downgraded.

findings.title: CORS allows any site
findings.why: Any website can call this API from a visitor's browser.
findings.fix: List the exact origins that need access with WithOrigins(...).

findings.title: GET /health is public and has no rate limit
findings.why: A public route without a limit can be flooded to slow the app down or to run up hosting costs.
findings.fix: Add .RequireRateLimiting("<policy>") with a policy partitioned by client.

findings.title: No central exception handler
findings.why: Unhandled errors can leak stack traces and internal names to callers.
